```{r}
source("../scripts/setup.R")

scenarios <- read.csv("../data/raw/cyber_expertise_diversity_survey_scenarios.csv")

alignment_scenarios_long <- read.csv("../data/processed/alignment_scenarios_long.csv")
max_alignment_scenarios_1_permutations <- read.csv("../data/processed/max_alignment_scenarios_1_permutations.csv")
max_alignment_scenarios_2_permutations <- read.csv("../data/processed/max_alignment_scenarios_2_permutations.csv")
max_alignment_scenarios_3_permutations <- read.csv("../data/processed/max_alignment_scenarios_3_permutations.csv")
max_alignment_scenarios_4_permutations <- read.csv("../data/processed/max_alignment_scenarios_4_permutations.csv")
max_alignment_scenarios_5_permutations <- read.csv("../data/processed/max_alignment_scenarios_5_permutations.csv")

max_alignment_scenarios <- max_alignment_scenarios_1_permutations |>
  bind_rows(max_alignment_scenarios_2_permutations) |> 
  bind_rows(max_alignment_scenarios_3_permutations) |> 
  bind_rows(max_alignment_scenarios_4_permutations) |> 
  bind_rows(max_alignment_scenarios_5_permutations) 

# GGplot defaults
theme_set(theme_minimal())

```

## Interdisciplinary cyber security

Understanding the value of diversity of expertise in cyber security requires a view of the problems that arise in cyber security, and the kinds of combinations of expertise that they require. For organisations, the utility of classifications of individuals into standardised specialisms depends on the extent to which it is possible to identify a need for particular kinds of individuals. Understanding how needs are aligned with specialisms means understanding the kinds of profiles of expertise that are required to address specific problems. The Cyber Expertise Diversity Survey elicited such profiles from participants, for a range of scenarios. While the dataset is limited, the presence of qualitative descriptions of these scenarios enables us to explore the ways in which scenarios map onto specialisms, in particular:

-   Which scenarios map straightforwardly onto one specialism

-   Which scenarios require combinations of specialisms

-   Which scenarios require significant expertise that is not accounted for by the specialisms

## Data analysis

### Looking at specialisms alignment with the scenarios

@fig-alignment-scenarios-overview shows that, overall, the Alignment index increases as we increase the number of permutations (this is, the scenarios are more interdisciplinary). While this could be expected, this is not the case for every scenario, as shown in @fig-alignment-scenarios, which provides a more nuanced view by displaying how the alignment score changes for every scenario.

```{r}
#| label: fig-alignment-scenarios-overview
#| fig-cap: "Alignment indices per number of permutations"
max_alignment_scenarios |> 
  mutate(
    n_permutations_txt = case_when(
      n_permutations == 1 ~ "No permutation",
      .default = paste(n_permutations, "Permutations")),
    n_permutations_txt = as.factor(n_permutations_txt),
    n_permutations_txt = fct_relevel(n_permutations_txt, "No permutation")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = alignment_index)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~n_permutations_txt, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Alignment index")
```

=

Explanation here.

```{r}
#| label: fig-alignment-scenarios
#| fig-cap: "Alignment indices per number of permutations and scenario"
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-align: "center"

scenario_names <- scenarios |> 
  select(scenario_name) |> 
  mutate(id = row_number())

max_alignment_scenarios |> 
  select(id, n_permutations, alignment_index) |> 
  left_join(scenario_names, by = join_by(id)) |>
  mutate(scenario_name = paste(id,"-", scenario_name),
         scenario_name = case_when(
           nchar(scenario_name) > 25 ~ paste0(str_sub(scenario_name, end = 25), "..."),
           .default = scenario_name),
         scenario_name = as.factor(scenario_name),
         scenario_name = fct_reorder(scenario_name, id)) |> 
  pivot_longer(alignment_index) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = n_permutations, y = value)) + 
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red")+ 
  # facet_wrap( ~id, ncol = 5, 
  #             labeller = as_labeller(
  #               function(string, suffix = scenario_names$scenario_name) paste(string, suffix)
  #             )) +   
  facet_wrap( ~scenario_name, ncol = 5) + 
  labs(title = "Alignment indices per number of permutations and scenario",
       y = "Scenario Alignment index",
       x = "Number of specialisms permutations")

```

### Questions for Viz

NB here we are looking at how well specialisms (including combinations of specialisms) are aligned with the scenarios people told us about. Before we were looking at how well people’s own profiles were aligned with the specialisms.

1.  The main thing is the kind of analysis that we sketched out in the slide above. Those two graphs show comparative views of the scenarios based on how the alignment changes when you are combining specialisms in greater numbers. Carlos and I were chatting about this last week and he said we might be able to do an interactive view of these to help explore the qualitative dataset (I.e. click on a specific point or line and it would tell you what the scenario number or name is, and then can look at the description). In the report we might just need to highlight a small number that are being referred to specifically, rather than necessarily embedding an interactive visualisation (which wouldn’t work well for a pdf/print version).

To make these graphs, there are csv files for 'max_alignment_scenarios_1_permutations', all the way up to 5 permutations. These are generated via the alignment_metric script.

One aspect of the data that we are losing here is: we are only looking at the categories of expertise that are included in CyBOK, and ignoring the additional categories that we added in. So one or two of them have very high alignment (17 and 23 for instance), but this is because these scenario were dominated by non-CyBOK categories of expertise, and the CyBOK ones had low values. To illuminate where this is the case, perhaps we could colour code the data points on the scatter to signal the fraction of expertise that was under CyBOK? This should be easy as it is just (sum of 'response' for that ID in 'comb_scenario' dataframe / sum of numeric fields for that ID in 'scenarios' dataframe, excluding the ID field itself)
:::

## Recommendations

## The path forward

Discussions of the professionalisation of cyber security are often motivated by analogies with professions such as accounting, medicine or law. However, it is important to recognise that professionalisation may take multiple pathways, that many professions do not end up tightly integrated, and that this destination may not always be the best or most appropriate. Clinical psychology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis and counselling are a case in point, with multiple career pathways, overlapping remits, multiple regulatory bodies and a history of failed attempts to better integrate.
